top.title: Senior Day: BYU will honor these 21 players on Saturday before hosting Cincinnati, although a few may return
top.description: BYU running back Lj Martin (4) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during overtime of an NCAA college football game against Kansas, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Lawrence, Kan. | Charlie Riedel, Associated Press Up to 21 BYU football players will make their final appearances at LaVell Edwards Stadium on Saturday before the No. 10 Cougars host Cincinnati in another pivotal Big 12 game. The players will be recognized on Senior Day (1:30 p.m. MST, Fox) for their contributions to the program in the final home game of the 2026 season and receive blankets from the school for their service to the team. Star running back LJ Martin, who is in his fourth season in Provo, is on the list, as expected. Appearing via Zoom in BYU’s weekly press briefing on Monday, Martin acknowledged that it will likely be his final game at LES, although technically he could return in 2027 via the NCAA’s new “age-based eligibility model” — commonly referred to as the “five-for-five” rule . “Yeah, this is probably my last time (playing at BYU),” Martin said. “I played four years here, had a lot of fun. Had a lot of great times. We’ll just see how things go. Just excited for the game Saturday. Haven’t really thought about it or anything. Just trying to go out there, focus on Saturday, just have a great game, and we’ll see where that goes.” Martin carried the ball a season-high 25 times for 127 yards and a touchdown in BYU’s 31-29 win over Kansas last weekend in his first significant playing time since sustaining a high ankle sprain on Oct. 3 at TCU. He said he was “just sore” on Sunday, but otherwise came out of the game “feeling pretty good” and looking forward to building on it. Martin seriously considered leaving BYU for the NFL last year after earning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year honors, but opted to stay after receiving input from the league on his projected draft status. He said he will go through the same process this year. “I will probably just talk to my parents, probably a couple guys here (at BYU), and just try to get feedback from the NFL, I guess,” he said. “Just kind of feel it out and see what I want to do with my future.” Also Monday, head coach Kalani Sitake recapped the three-overtime win over Kansas , said an almost healthy Martin made a huge difference for an offense that had struggled to run the football in recent weeks, and looked ahead to facing a Cincinnati team (6-5, 3-5) that snapped a three-game losing skid with a 35-28 win over Colorado last Saturday. “It was good to see LJ back to his old self,” Sitake said. “I think that last (touchdown) run was probably the LJ that we’ve been waiting for. Two weeks ago (vs. Baylor) he got stepped on, and last week he got pulled on, on that (surgically repaired) leg. I can’t wait to see him roll this Saturday.” BYU players who will be recognized Saturday Along with Martin, other offensive players who will be recognized on Saturday include receiver Tiger Bachmeier, quarterback Treyson Bourguet, offensive lineman

top.title: Georgia Tech Coach Brent Key Promises Fight Against UGA Rivalry
top.description: Ashley Tumlin-Imagn Images The Georgia Bulldogs are heading into their annual rivalry game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets with a massive lead in the standings. Georgia finished the SEC schedule on top and is set for its sixth straight conference title game appearance. This matchup is known as Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, but the dynamic has shifted significantly this year. Georgia Tech enters the game as a heavy underdog, facing a Georgia team that has dominated the series. The Jackets have lost the last eight games in this rivalry. Despite the lopsided history, Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key says his team refuses to roll over. He knows the Bulldogs well, and he knows his squad must execute a solid game plan to have any chance. A Season of Struggles The Yellow Jackets fell to Wake Forest at home in a 50-29 defeat. Wake Forest opened the game with 29 straight points and held the Jackets to just seven points in the first half. The defense allowed 607 total yards of offense, including 258 rushing yards for the opposing team. Georgia Tech turned the ball over three times, a mistake that cost them any hope of a comeback. Offensively, the Jackets struggled to find a rhythm until the second half. However, these individual efforts were not enough to overcome the defensive breakdowns. The team only averaged 6.3 yards per pass and failed to record a single sack against Wake Forest. Key’s Honest Assessment He acknowledged the difficulty of the task but promised his team would compete. “We’re going to show up, promise you that,” Key said. He emphasized that this is the most important game for his program because it is an in-state rivalry. Georgia Tech might still lose at Sanford Stadium even if they deliver their finest performance. The Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country, and they are looking to finish strong. Georgia Tech fans want to believe their team can cause a shock, but the reality of the season makes that unlikely. The Jackets have taken a significant step back, yet they remain dangerous if Georgia loses focus.

top.title: Kyle McCord’s 32.6 Rating Shows Miami Needs A Real Plan
top.description: Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Miami Dolphins fans saw a rough Sunday in Orchard Park as the team fell 26-9 to the Buffalo Bills. The final score looked close for a while, but the offense could not get going when it mattered most. Quarterback Kyle McCord threw for just 102 yards and one interception in his second start. Through Sunday’s games, the league’s lowest passer rating belonged to a quarterback at 32.6. The defense did enough to keep the game within reach for a long time. Safety Zayne Anderson earned a 90.8 grade from PFF for his work covering a short-handed secondary. An interception, a sack, and three pass breakups were his final stats. That effort helped hold Buffalo to field goals on three of their five red-zone trips. The Defense Stands Tall While the offense struggled, the defensive unit played with real energy. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez led the team with 13 combined tackles and added an interception. With 93 tackles, he currently holds the 7th spot in the National Football League. The group forced Josh Allen to throw two interceptions on the day. Head Coach Jeff Hafley explained the strategy against the Bills’ star quarterback. “We pressured him early and gave him a lot of different looks,” Hafley said of the plan against Allen, according to Yahoo Sports . He added that the rush and coverage worked well but noted there is still room for growth. “Rush plus coverage, I think that’s a pretty good day against Josh. But we can do better.” Offensive Woes Continue The offense could not take advantage of the defensive stops. Miami went 2 for 14 on third down and never reached the end zone. New kicker Daniel Carlson made all three of his field goals to score all nine of Miami’s points. Two of those kicks came from 52 yards out. McCord knew the offense was not close to good enough to win. “It’s tough to win games when you’re kicking field goals all day,” McCord said after the game. His receivers also had a tough time, with Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas combining for five drops. Douglas was targeted 10 times but only caught two passes for 30 yards. Hafley addressed the rookie receiver’s struggles after the loss. “Young player. It was one of those days,” Hafley said of Douglas. The coach noted that the play could have been huge for the rookie. “It could have been another huge day for him. It wasn’t.” The Dolphins now sit at 1-9 on the season after the loss. The team has shown they can fight, but they need more from their offense to win games. The front office will have to decide how much help to add around the quarterback this offseason. While time remains for growth for both Bell and Douglas, the front office will gain clearer insight this offseason regarding receiver additions needed around the drafted quarterback. Miami faces the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at Hard Rock Stadium.

top.title: Women’s World Cup returns to U.S. in 2031 with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts
top.description: FIFA Women's World Cup hosting announcement What happened? The Women’s World Cup is coming back to the United States for the first time since 2003, and it’ll be the biggest edition yet. FIFA awarded the 2031 tournament to the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica on Monday, marking the first time four countries will share hosting duties. The field will expand to 48 teams, with 104 matches on the schedule. FIFA also named the United Kingdom as host of the 2035 Women’s World Cup. 'Biggest most impactful Women's World Cup in history' 'Biggest most impactful Women's World Cup in history' In 2003, Cindy Parlow Cone scored in the USWNT’s World Cup opener against Sweden at RFK Stadium. Twenty-three years later, she was in Zurich as U.S. Soccer President, looking ahead to what the tournament’s return could mean for the next generation of players. “We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup,” Cone said. “This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women’s World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women’s soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.” What this means for the U.S. and the other federations While the U.S. has hosted Women's World Cups in the past, it hasn't done so since 2003. Before that, it was the 1999 Women's World Cup. While the U.S. have been here before, this is the first time that Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will be hosting the women's tournament. "We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players," U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson said. What's next? What's next? The 2031 Women’s World Cup will come five years after the men’s tournament in North America and three years after the Los Angeles Olympics. U.S. Soccer sees a chance to build on both events and bring more fans to the women’s game. With the four host countries set, the next question is which cities will get games. The joint bid put forward more than 30 candidates, and U.S. Soccer says the host cities and stadiums will be announced as planning moves forward.

top.title: Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
top.description: It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski. Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record. But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate. His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history. The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year. Tarkowski's dismissal proved a big talking point during and after the match, with opinions split on whether he should have gone. Even Moyes wasn't sure. He told BBC Match of the Day: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that." James Tarkowski received his first Premier League red card [Getty Images] Why did Tarkowski get sent off? So what exactly happened? Just 15 minutes after Keane Lewis-Potter scored his second deflected strike of the evening, Everton skipper Tarkowski thundered into a challenge on Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk. He won the ball but also followed through with the challenge forcefully. Initially, referee Craig Pawson deemed a foul and a yellow card was enough. But, after an intervention from the video assistant referee (VAR) and studying the replay, Pawson changed the yellow for a red. The Premier League match centre said on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play. "VAR: 'Point of contact is on the shin. He's got speed and intensity. Studs are high.' "REF: 'After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card - and a red card.'" 'Game's gone' or '100% red'? Experts are split Referees are asked to take into account several considerations for what counts as serious foul play including the speed of the challenge, its intensity, force and what degree of control there was. But, as always, there was plenty of debate about whether it was the correct decision. BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, said: "Really not sure about this as a VAR red card. "Yes, Tarkowski absolutely ticks the boxes for speed and intensity and leading high with studs showing. "But the question marks are that Tarkowski made only small contact and didn't have a straight leg when he did so. "Maybe his reputation played a part? Remember, he wrongly escaped a VAR red card against Liverpool for a challenge, which was along the same lines. He won the ball and then followed through into Alexis Mac Allister

top.title: Brentford hit Everton for four to soar into Premier League top six
top.description: Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice in Brentford's win over Everton (Adrian DENNIS) Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday. Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match. Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday. "It'll probably go a bit under the radar because of the sending off but 11 versus 11 we were outstanding," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews. "I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. "Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it." David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table. "With two shots, both deflected in and took the goalkeeper the wrong way, and the third goal was a worldie outside the box. We could use them as excuses but there's no excuses tonight," said Moyes. "The performance was way below the standards we've set and the way we've been playing recently." A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford. Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally. The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball. Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin. Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool. Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago. Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half. The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time. Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute. Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils. United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years. kca/iwd

top.title: Kerby Joseph escapes debut with 'no red flags,' good to go vs Bears
top.description: Kerby Joseph's season debut went off without a hitch, and the Detroit Lions safety looks ready to play on short rest on Thanksgiving against the Chicago Bears. "There’s no red flags, so that’s a good sign," Lions coach Dan Campbell said Monday, Nov. 23. "He got over 40 reps, so that was good. That’s a good sign. And so he’ll be better for those reps, just like [Brian] Branch was to get his first set of reps for the season." Joseph played 46 snaps (67%) as the Lions' third safety in Sunday's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , his first game since October 2025 because of a cartilage condition in his knee. BAND OF BROTHERS: How Lions defense has come together to suddenly be one of NFL's stingiest units He made one tackle on a bubble screen, was credited with another when he tagged Baker Mayfield down after a scramble and lined up almost exclusively as a deep safety in the Lions' nickel package, with Branch and Chuck Clark also on the field. Campbell said last week Joseph looked good in practice, but the Lions needed to see how he responded to back-to-back days of work and how he recovered from game action before deciding how to use him going forward. Clark wore the green-dot defensive communication helmet and played every snap against the Bucs , and Branch, who returned last month from a torn Achilles suffered late in the 2025 season, was on the field for 68 of 69 defensive plays. The Lions play the Bears on Thursday (1 p.m., CBS) with three days rest this week, then have a long weekend before getting into the homestretch of their schedule with games against the Atlanta Falcons, Tennessee Titans , Minnesota Vikings , New York Giants , Bears again and Green Bay Packers . "I thought he did some good things," Campbell said. "There’s things that he’s going to only just get better at now that he’s been out there and I thought it was pretty good. I mean, when you’re able to get he and BB on the field and you got Chuck out there, it’s a pretty good unit." Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. top.title: Jameson Williams Responds to Controversial Touchdown Flip
top.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams has never been shy about showing off his personality, but his latest touchdown celebration had plenty of fans holding their breath. During Sunday’s 31-21 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field, Williams hauled in a 57-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff before launching himself into a front flip as he crossed the goal line. The problem? Williams didn’t exactly stick the landing, and the timing couldn’t have been much worse considering what happened to teammate Aidan Hutchinson just one week earlier. Following the game, Williams was asked about his decision to attempt the risky celebration. His response was about as Jameson Williams as it gets. Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) makes a catch for a touchdown against Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jameson Williams Explains His Controversial Celebration Speaking with reporters following Detroit’s sixth consecutive victory, Williams admitted that the flip wasn’t exactly something he had carefully planned. “The flip was, like, an in-the-moment thing, I ain’t gonna lie,” Williams said, according to The Detroit News . Williams also acknowledged that he hadn’t been entirely sure what to do as he approached the end zone. Fortunately, the awkward landing didn’t prevent him from finishing the game. But here’s where things get interesting. According to Parker Hurley of Heavy , Williams apparently has no intention of permanently retiring the celebration. “I’m going to try to land one later in the year for y’all, for sure,” Williams said. Yep, it sounds like Jamo might give it another shot. Aidan Hutchinson’s Injury Makes Williams’ Flip More Concerning The controversy surrounding Williams’ celebration stems from what happened to Hutchinson during Detroit’s November 15 victory over the New England Patriots in Germany. Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL after jumping into the air and landing awkwardly while celebrating a sack. The devastating injury immediately sparked conversations about whether NFL players should reconsider potentially dangerous celebrations. However, Lions head coach Dan Campbell made his position on touchdown celebrations clear , explaining that he wasn’t interested in policing how his players celebrate. That doesn’t necessarily mean Williams’ flip was a great idea, particularly with Detroit preparing for an important Thanksgiving showdown against the Chicago Bears. Williams has become one of Detroit’s most dangerous offensive weapons, and the Lions certainly can’t afford to lose another impact player because of an unnecessary injury. Of course, Williams’ performance Sunday provided another reminder of why he’s so valuable to Detroit’s offense. top.title: Here are the Big Ten’s 4 paths for Indiana to reach its championship game
top.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - DECEMBER 06: Head coach Curt Cignetti of the Indiana Hoosiers lifts the trophy after defeating the Ohio State Buckeyes 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Football Championship at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 06, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Indiana football, despite a pair of losses in conference play, is still alive in the race for a bid in the Big Ten Championship Game. The game, set for Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, will be the league’s last. Conference title games will be discontinued under the newly-expanded College Football Playoff starting with the 2027 season. This is the Hoosiers’ last chance to win another conference championship in their home state. Indiana is still alive, but doesn’t control its own destiny. There’s too many teams bunched around the top for the Hoosiers to make it in with just a win over Purdue, but said win is vital to their chances. top.title: Atlanta Dream Must Fix Roster Flaws Before 2027 Season
top.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, leaving the Dream one win short of a championship. While the franchise reached its first Finals since 2013, the path to a title demands more than just repeating the same roster. Shooting Woes Stopped the Dream Atlanta was elite in several categories last year, including rebounding and defense, yet the team could not close out the series. The main issue was shooting beyond the arc. The Dream ranked 11th overall in 3-point shooting percentage at 32.5 percent, a number too low for a contender. Even star players struggled to find their rhythm when it mattered most. Rhyne Howard shot 35.5 percent during the regular season but dropped to 30.4 percent in the postseason. Angel Reese and Jordin Canada also missed their marks from deep, with percentages of 19.3 and 29.2 respectively. General manager Dan Padover proved his worth by landing Angel Reese, but that single move is not enough to beat the best teams in the league. High Post Hoops notes that while Padover touches gold, the roster needs a dedicated 3-point shooter to balance the attack. Retaining DeWanna Bonner would help, but the team needs more depth to survive a grueling schedule. Adding a player like Chennedy Carter could be a high-risk, high-reward move that changes the dynamic of the bench. Ownership and Arena Logistics The team faces business hurdles that may affect on‑court performance unless they are addressed. The Dream will move all 25 home games to State Farm Arena in 2027, a shift that requires careful planning. The 2026 postseason created a logistical headache because the venue already had major events booked. To prevent another chaotic scramble, the league has instituted strict rules for the 2027 season. Teams that fail to report these issues risk losing home playoff games or facing financial fines. A Sisterhood Built to Last The team president said the journey mattered beyond the final score. Morgan Shaw Parker, the team President and Chief Operating Officer, thanked fans for their support during the championship run. In a letter to supporters, she emphasized the bond formed within the city. “We didn’t just rebuild a basketball team. We rebuilt a connection with our city,” she wrote, according to CBS News . Despite admitting the letdown, Parker encouraged supporters to appreciate the community that grew around the franchise. She also highlighted the long-term vision for the organization despite the missing trophy. “We may not have finished this season with a championship, but we have built a franchise Atlanta can be proud of, a community worth protecting, and a sisterhood worth believing in,” she wrote.

top.title: Talor Gooch Faces Harsh Reality As LIV Golf Folds
top.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Talor Gooch secured four wins and over $72 million in prize money during the LIV Golf era, yet he now faces a stark silence regarding his future. The 35-year-old finds himself in a unique position where past financial success offers little protection against current exclusion. The road back to the PGA Tour looks incredibly steep for the former RSM Classic winner. He has played in six majors since LIV began in 2022, missing the cut three times and never finishing higher than 34th. That track record does not inspire confidence among tournament directors who have the power to grant invites. A Different Path Than Chacarra Other defectors are finding success by returning to competitive golf, but their stories highlight Gooch’s struggle. Full exempt status on the PGA Tour for 2027 is held by Eugenio Chacarra, who secured three victories on the DP World Tour in 2026. Chacarra admitted he lost motivation while on LIV but regained his hunger after leaving the Saudi-backed circuit. “You know, I lost those things my last year with LIV, and I earned it back by leaving, by working hard, by showing the world what I’m capable of, and I’m more hungry than ever,” Chacarra said. Chacarra plans to face 33 players ahead of him in the world rankings as he aims for the Ryder Cup. He has a clear plan to get better over the next 30 days before his first start at Torrey Pines. Gooch lacks this kind of clear momentum. He took on a leadership role for LIV after Brooks Koepka left, rebranding his team to OKGC, but that leadership role dissolved when the league itself folded. Uncertain Future for the Leader Not every player wants to grind through a full global schedule, and some are choosing a lighter load. Marc Leishman, a former Ripper GC teammate of Cameron Smith, said he is “past the grind” of being away from his family for more than half the year. Ahead of the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney, Leishman stated to reporters that he holds no regrets regarding his decision to join LIV despite the uncertainty surrounding his future. “Obviously, it’s a little uncertain what the future holds for me, but if I knew exactly what was going to happen, I would have made the same decision. I’ve certainly got no regrets,” Leishman said. Instead of pursuing a full card, Leishman intends to focus on major championships and events in his homeland. Gooch does not have this luxury. He was once a figure of ridicule for comparing LIV events to the Ryder Cup, despite never having played in either. The silence surrounding his next move suggests the golf world has moved on. He is third on LIV’s all-time money list, but that ranking holds little value in the current landscape.

There’s one award, however, that already has a lot of people sweating over who might take home the hardware. The NFL Comeback Player of the Year award. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed. nigeria.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
nigeria.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. nigeria.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. nigeria.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price. The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20. The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday. Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market. Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier. Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025. Self-mining margins stay thin Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year earlier, with another 28.7 exahashes per second of co-mining at third-party sites, the quarterly report shows . The economics are tight. Self-mining generated $217.5 million in revenue in the quarter but only $6.2 million in gross profit. Electricity averaged $47 per megawatt-hour, and the fleet ran at 15.4 joules per terahash. Bitdeer posted record revenue of $320.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $69.6 million, but a net loss of $125.5 million. That included a $54.6 million non-cash loss tied to a bitcoin-collateralized loan from a related party. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. sports.title: Kyle McCord’s 32.6 Rating Shows Miami Needs A Real Plan
sports.description: Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Miami Dolphins fans saw a rough Sunday in Orchard Park as the team fell 26-9 to the Buffalo Bills. The final score looked close for a while, but the offense could not get going when it mattered most. Quarterback Kyle McCord threw for just 102 yards and one interception in his second start. Through Sunday’s games, the league’s lowest passer rating belonged to a quarterback at 32.6. The defense did enough to keep the game within reach for a long time. Safety Zayne Anderson earned a 90.8 grade from PFF for his work covering a short-handed secondary. An interception, a sack, and three pass breakups were his final stats. That effort helped hold Buffalo to field goals on three of their five red-zone trips. The Defense Stands Tall While the offense struggled, the defensive unit played with real energy. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez led the team with 13 combined tackles and added an interception. With 93 tackles, he currently holds the 7th spot in the National Football League. The group forced Josh Allen to throw two interceptions on the day. Head Coach Jeff Hafley explained the strategy against the Bills’ star quarterback. “We pressured him early and gave him a lot of different looks,” Hafley said of the plan against Allen, according to Yahoo Sports . He added that the rush and coverage worked well but noted there is still room for growth. “Rush plus coverage, I think that’s a pretty good day against Josh. But we can do better.” Offensive Woes Continue The offense could not take advantage of the defensive stops. Miami went 2 for 14 on third down and never reached the end zone. New kicker Daniel Carlson made all three of his field goals to score all nine of Miami’s points. Two of those kicks came from 52 yards out. McCord knew the offense was not close to good enough to win. “It’s tough to win games when you’re kicking field goals all day,” McCord said after the game. His receivers also had a tough time, with Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas combining for five drops. Douglas was targeted 10 times but only caught two passes for 30 yards. Hafley addressed the rookie receiver’s struggles after the loss. “Young player. It was one of those days,” Hafley said of Douglas. The coach noted that the play could have been huge for the rookie. “It could have been another huge day for him. It wasn’t.” The Dolphins now sit at 1-9 on the season after the loss. The team has shown they can fight, but they need more from their offense to win games. The front office will have to decide how much help to add around the quarterback this offseason. While time remains for growth for both Bell and Douglas, the front office will gain clearer insight this offseason regarding receiver additions needed around the drafted quarterback. Miami faces the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at Hard Rock Stadium.

sports.title: Women’s World Cup returns to U.S. in 2031 with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica as co-hosts
sports.description: FIFA Women's World Cup hosting announcement What happened? The Women’s World Cup is coming back to the United States for the first time since 2003, and it’ll be the biggest edition yet. FIFA awarded the 2031 tournament to the U.S., Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica on Monday, marking the first time four countries will share hosting duties. The field will expand to 48 teams, with 104 matches on the schedule. FIFA also named the United Kingdom as host of the 2035 Women’s World Cup. 'Biggest most impactful Women's World Cup in history' 'Biggest most impactful Women's World Cup in history' In 2003, Cindy Parlow Cone scored in the USWNT’s World Cup opener against Sweden at RFK Stadium. Twenty-three years later, she was in Zurich as U.S. Soccer President, looking ahead to what the tournament’s return could mean for the next generation of players. “We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup,” Cone said. “This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women’s World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women’s soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.” What this means for the U.S. and the other federations While the U.S. has hosted Women's World Cups in the past, it hasn't done so since 2003. Before that, it was the 1999 Women's World Cup. While the U.S. have been here before, this is the first time that Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will be hosting the women's tournament. "We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players," U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson said. What's next? What's next? The 2031 Women’s World Cup will come five years after the men’s tournament in North America and three years after the Los Angeles Olympics. U.S. Soccer sees a chance to build on both events and bring more fans to the women’s game. With the four host countries set, the next question is which cities will get games. The joint bid put forward more than 30 candidates, and U.S. Soccer says the host cities and stadiums will be announced as planning moves forward.

sports.title: Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
sports.description: It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski. Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record. But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate. His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history. The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year. Tarkowski's dismissal proved a big talking point during and after the match, with opinions split on whether he should have gone. Even Moyes wasn't sure. He told BBC Match of the Day: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that." James Tarkowski received his first Premier League red card [Getty Images] Why did Tarkowski get sent off? So what exactly happened? Just 15 minutes after Keane Lewis-Potter scored his second deflected strike of the evening, Everton skipper Tarkowski thundered into a challenge on Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk. He won the ball but also followed through with the challenge forcefully. Initially, referee Craig Pawson deemed a foul and a yellow card was enough. But, after an intervention from the video assistant referee (VAR) and studying the replay, Pawson changed the yellow for a red. The Premier League match centre said on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play. "VAR: 'Point of contact is on the shin. He's got speed and intensity. Studs are high.' "REF: 'After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card - and a red card.'" 'Game's gone' or '100% red'? Experts are split Referees are asked to take into account several considerations for what counts as serious foul play including the speed of the challenge, its intensity, force and what degree of control there was. But, as always, there was plenty of debate about whether it was the correct decision. BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, said: "Really not sure about this as a VAR red card. "But the question marks are that Tarkowski made only small contact and didn't have a straight leg when he did so. "Maybe his reputation played a part? sports.title: Brentford hit Everton for four to soar into Premier League top six
sports.description: Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice in Brentford's win over Everton (Adrian DENNIS) Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday. Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match. Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday. "It'll probably go a bit under the radar because of the sending off but 11 versus 11 we were outstanding," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews. "I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. "Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it." David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table. "With two shots, both deflected in and took the goalkeeper the wrong way, and the third goal was a worldie outside the box. We could use them as excuses but there's no excuses tonight," said Moyes. "The performance was way below the standards we've set and the way we've been playing recently." A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford. Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally. The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball. Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin. Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool. Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago. Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half. The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time. Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute. Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils. The problem? Williams didn’t exactly stick the landing, and the timing couldn’t have been much worse considering what happened to teammate Aidan Hutchinson just one week earlier. sports.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Willie Green and Dusty May share a connection that goes far beyond a standard coach and assistant role. The Dallas Mavericks have found a rare spark in their leadership pair, one that started on a golf course in Michigan. The bond influences the team’s culture. They hit it off immediately, acting like long-lost friends from their first meeting. That instant chemistry is now the foundation of a 10-7 team heading into Tuesday’s NBA Cup game in Denver. A Golf Outing That Changed Everything Their story began when a mutual friend invited both men to play golf in Michigan. sports.title: Atlanta Dream Must Fix Roster Flaws Before 2027 Season
sports.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, leaving the Dream one win short of a championship. While the franchise reached its first Finals since 2013, the path to a title demands more than just repeating the same roster. Shooting Woes Stopped the Dream Atlanta was elite in several categories last year, including rebounding and defense, yet the team could not close out the series. The main issue was shooting beyond the arc. The Dream ranked 11th overall in 3-point shooting percentage at 32.5 percent, a number too low for a contender. Even star players struggled to find their rhythm when it mattered most. Rhyne Howard shot 35.5 percent during the regular season but dropped to 30.4 percent in the postseason. Angel Reese and Jordin Canada also missed their marks from deep, with percentages of 19.3 and 29.2 respectively. General manager Dan Padover proved his worth by landing Angel Reese, but that single move is not enough to beat the best teams in the league. High Post Hoops notes that while Padover touches gold, the roster needs a dedicated 3-point shooter to balance the attack. Retaining DeWanna Bonner would help, but the team needs more depth to survive a grueling schedule. Adding a player like Chennedy Carter could be a high-risk, high-reward move that changes the dynamic of the bench. Ownership and Arena Logistics The team faces business hurdles that may affect on‑court performance unless they are addressed. The Dream will move all 25 home games to State Farm Arena in 2027, a shift that requires careful planning. The 2026 postseason created a logistical headache because the venue already had major events booked. To prevent another chaotic scramble, the league has instituted strict rules for the 2027 season. Teams that fail to report these issues risk losing home playoff games or facing financial fines. A Sisterhood Built to Last The team president said the journey mattered beyond the final score. Morgan Shaw Parker, the team President and Chief Operating Officer, thanked fans for their support during the championship run. In a letter to supporters, she emphasized the bond formed within the city. “We didn’t just rebuild a basketball team. We rebuilt a connection with our city,” she wrote, according to CBS News . Despite admitting the letdown, Parker encouraged supporters to appreciate the community that grew around the franchise. She also highlighted the long-term vision for the organization despite the missing trophy. “We may not have finished this season with a championship, but we have built a franchise Atlanta can be proud of, a community worth protecting, and a sisterhood worth believing in,” she wrote.

sports.title: Talor Gooch Faces Harsh Reality As LIV Golf Folds
sports.description: John (Jack) Power-Imagn Images Talor Gooch secured four wins and over $72 million in prize money during the LIV Golf era, yet he now faces a stark silence regarding his future. The 35-year-old finds himself in a unique position where past financial success offers little protection against current exclusion. The road back to the PGA Tour looks incredibly steep for the former RSM Classic winner. He has played in six majors since LIV began in 2022, missing the cut three times and never finishing higher than 34th. That track record does not inspire confidence among tournament directors who have the power to grant invites. A Different Path Than Chacarra Other defectors are finding success by returning to competitive golf, but their stories highlight Gooch’s struggle. Full exempt status on the PGA Tour for 2027 is held by Eugenio Chacarra, who secured three victories on the DP World Tour in 2026. Chacarra admitted he lost motivation while on LIV but regained his hunger after leaving the Saudi-backed circuit. “You know, I lost those things my last year with LIV, and I earned it back by leaving, by working hard, by showing the world what I’m capable of, and I’m more hungry than ever,” Chacarra said. Chacarra plans to face 33 players ahead of him in the world rankings as he aims for the Ryder Cup. He has a clear plan to get better over the next 30 days before his first start at Torrey Pines. Gooch lacks this kind of clear momentum. He took on a leadership role for LIV after Brooks Koepka left, rebranding his team to OKGC, but that leadership role dissolved when the league itself folded. Uncertain Future for the Leader Not every player wants to grind through a full global schedule, and some are choosing a lighter load. Marc Leishman, a former Ripper GC teammate of Cameron Smith, said he is “past the grind” of being away from his family for more than half the year. Ahead of the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney, Leishman stated to reporters that he holds no regrets regarding his decision to join LIV despite the uncertainty surrounding his future. “Obviously, it’s a little uncertain what the future holds for me, but if I knew exactly what was going to happen, I would have made the same decision. I’ve certainly got no regrets,” Leishman said. Instead of pursuing a full card, Leishman intends to focus on major championships and events in his homeland. Gooch does not have this luxury. He was once a figure of ridicule for comparing LIV events to the Ryder Cup, despite never having played in either. The silence surrounding his next move suggests the golf world has moved on. He is third on LIV’s all-time money list, but that ranking holds little value in the current landscape.

technology.title: Inception - possibly a ShinyHunters reboot - claims seven victims in a week
technology.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media. On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims. None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register ’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information. Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions. In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.” The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added. technology.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
technology.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

technology.description: Imagine something as mission-critical as the brakes on a trailer being vulnerable to unauthorized control. One Australian manufacturer made the interesting choice of building Bluetooth into a trailer brake controller without adequately securing its critical braking functions. Anyone within Bluetooth range of an unpatched Elecbrakes trailer controller could potentially trigger its brakes or apply more braking force than intended, without needing to authenticate. The discovery comes courtesy of a pair of security researchers from Element Digital, Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy. Their investigation began earlier this year when Forck was driving down the road and noticed that his physical Elecbrakes In-Car Remote had connected to someone else's trailer without pairing or prompting him. “It had connected mid-drive, without pairing or a prompt, to a brake controller that wasn’t mine, on a trailer I’d never seen, belonging to a driver who had no idea,” the researchers wrote . That one-off connection triggered a full-scale investigation by the pair. For those unfamiliar with trailer brake controllers, these devices are commonly used on larger trailers. Australian manufacturer Elecbrakes sells such controllers in Australia and New Zealand. Depending on jurisdiction, trailers over a certain weight are required to have their own braking system, which Elecbrakes manufactures. Elecbrakes offers two versions that are designed to be easier to install than traditional controllers: One that’s mounted in a vehicle, and one that is mounted directly on a trailer. That trailer-mounted unit can receive Bluetooth commands from the Elecbrakes smartphone app or a separate in-car remote. Given the importance of such control units to road safety, it’s easy to imagine how serious such a vulnerability could be if it proved to be easy to exploit, and boy, did it. Forck and McCarthy admitted they’re infrastructure security guys, not software devs, so they turned to Claude Code to dissect a decompiled copy of the Elecbrakes app, which Claude was happy to oblige. “What came back from the analysis was a map of the device’s entire Bluetooth GATT profile: 47 characteristics across four services, commands sent as plain unencrypted byte arrays, no checksums, no sequence numbers,” the researchers noted. To make matters worse, there was no authentication required for critical braking commands, even though other Bluetooth functions required pairing. science.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.
